title: Hom into an essentially constant ind-system value is the colimit of Hom sets
statement: Let $J$ be a filtered category, $\mathcal C$ a category, and $F:J\to\mathcal C$ a diagram that is essentially constant as an ind-object with value $X$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram]. For every object $Y$ of $\mathcal C$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(Y,F(j))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(Y,X)$ induced by the cocone maps $p_j:F(j)\to X$ of the essential constancy is a bijection.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0FND, label lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, proof line 9515, first equality; Categories Tag 05PY, label categories-lemma-characterize-essentially-constant-ind

proof.text: Write p_j : F(j) \to X for the natural maps supplied by essential constancy. The canonical map from the filtered colimit sends the class of a morphism f : Y \to F(j) to p_j composed with f; naturality of the p_j makes this independent of the representative and defines a map into Hom_C(Y,X).

source.place: Tag 05PY, characterization of essentially constant ind-diagrams

proof.text: For surjectivity, let g : Y \to X. The chosen section s : X \to F(j0) gives the representative s composed with g at j0, and p_{j0} composed with s is the identity of X, so its image is g.

For injectivity, suppose f : Y \to F(j) and f' : Y \to F(j') have equal images in Hom_C(Y,X), so p_j composed with f equals p_{j'} composed with f'. Choose, by filteredness, an index k receiving maps from j, j' and j0. Applying filteredness once more if needed lets the factorization clause of the definition be used for both transition maps into one common stage k.

source.place: Tag 05PY, characterization of essentially constant ind-diagrams

proof.text: At that common stage, the two transition composites are respectively (F(j0) \to F(k)) composed with s composed with p_j and (F(j0) \to F(k)) composed with s composed with p_{j'}. Postcomposing f and f' therefore gives equal arrows because p_j composed with f equals p_{j'} composed with f'. The two representatives agree at a later stage and define the same colimit class, proving injectivity.

source.place: Tag 05PY, characterization of essentially constant ind-diagrams

proof.text: The construction is compatible with postcomposition in Y and with morphisms of essentially constant diagrams, so the resulting bijection is the stated canonical one.
